name: Ghostfeed
subcategory: AI UGC reaction videos + TikTok photo slideshows
tagline: Drops your AI avatar into a real creator's reaction clip, builds TikTok photo slideshows, and posts them

pricing.notes: Growth is the highlighted tier, 49 USD against a 69 USD list price. Credits are the real meter: 300 credits, 1 credit = 1 second of video or 1 image, so roughly 50 short videos. Starter is 29 USD for 150 credits, Agency 99 USD for 700.
pricing.freeTier: The free plan carries no video credits: one slideshow project with three variants, the reaction library, posting and MCP access, and nothing that renders video.

verdictSummary: None of the pixels here come from a model Ghostfeed trained. The reaction flow is two hosted API calls in a trench coat: an image-edit model puts your avatar into the first frame of an existing clip, then an image-to-video model animates that frame, either cloning the reference motion or following a prompt. A builder with a fal.ai key and ffmpeg gets a working version of that loop over a weekend, and pays the per-second model invoices either way. What does not fall out of a weekend is the boring half · a template library already cropped to 9:16 with the motion tagged, an avatar that survives twenty renders looking like the same person, a credit ledger that refunds you when a render hangs, and a TikTok publishing app that took platform review to get. Build it for yourself and it works · run it daily for a brand and you rebuild the plumbing instead.
coreLoopDIY: Put an avatar photo into the first frame of a reaction clip with a hosted image-edit model, approve that frame, then animate it with a hosted image-to-video model and burn the hook text over the result.
requirements: fal.ai or Replicate API key for the image-edit and image-to-video models
reaction clips you have the right to reuse
an always-on box for the render queue
whatYouLose: a reaction-template library already cropped to 9:16 with the motion tagged, instead of clips you source yourself
avatar consistency · the same face and lighting across twenty renders, not twenty cousins
a credit ledger that refunds a hung or failed render · DIY eats every model invoice
TikTok publishing and scheduling through an OAuth app that already passed platform review
the slideshow text-layout engine and variant rotation that turns one deck into a week of posts
moatNotes: tuned per-model prompt pipelines and platform-review pain, not a model of their own
whyPeopleStillPay: The models underneath churn every few weeks · pricing, aspect-ratio quirks, content filters, and which one currently holds a face steady for five seconds. The subscription outsources that treadmill and converts unpredictable per-second render invoices into one known number, with the failed renders refunded rather than billed. It also arrives with a TikTok publishing app that already cleared review, which is weeks a solo builder spends before posting anything.

notes: Submitted by the founder · verdict written against the honest DIY, and the DIY here is real, so it is a kinda.
prompt:
Build me a personal UGC reaction video factory to replace Ghostfeed. Requirements:

- Node + Express + better-sqlite3, a localhost dashboard with three panes: my
  avatar photos, a folder of reaction clips I own, and a render queue.
- First frame: pull frame 0 from a chosen clip with ffmpeg, send it plus my
  avatar photo to fal.ai's image-edit queue API, prompt it to swap the person
  and hold the pose, framing, and lighting. Keep that prompt in
  prompts/first-frame.txt so I can tune it without touching code.
- Nothing animates until I approve the frame, so give me approve, regenerate,
  and discard buttons · the frame costs cents and the video costs dollars.
- Motion: on approve, submit the frame to fal.ai's image-to-video queue (Kling)
  with either the reference clip's motion or a text prompt, poll until done,
  write the mp4 to media/, and store the real dollar cost on the row.
- Burn the hook line over the top third with ffmpeg drawtext, 1080x1920 out,
  clear of the TikTok UI safe area.
- Slideshow mode: a folder of images plus one hook line each, exported with
  sharp as 1080x1920 PNGs numbered in post order.
- A node-cron tick retries failures 3 times with backoff and marks the row
  before submitting, so a retry never double-bills me.
- FAL_KEY in .env. No accounts, no telemetry, everything on my disk except the
  model calls.
- Out of scope: posting to TikTok (that OAuth review takes weeks · export the
  mp4 and upload by hand) and teams. Only ingest clips I have the right to use.
- README: getting a fal.ai key, what one 5-second render costs, and where media
  lands on disk.
